title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Livelihoods, Innovation, Food Security and Entrepreneurship (LIFE) programme will work in Grand Bassa and Riversess counties, Liberia. It aims to contribute to Concern Liberia's Food Systems for Food Security thematic programme, and the goal of the grant is to increase rural economic development and food security in Liberia. The programme will support over 51,375 people living in extreme poor households including those headed by women, households with disabled members, landless households, households with children under five. This will be done through increasing access to agricultural extension and advisory services, increased adoption and diffusion of climate-smart adaptation practices by smallholder and subsistence farmers and, agriculture cooperatives, and women and youth groups.. RM 2 Adaptation: Installation of systems that enable significant energy savings compared to older systems and measures to design and deliver water and sanitation services which reduce vulnerability to floods of affected water and sanitation infrastructure through the establishment of water points and strengthened savings and loans groups. DRR 1: This outcome focues on improving resilience among farmers and communities by establishing two key community level structures, community savings and loans associations and We Are One support groups. Efforts are made to ensure strengthened ownership of these by community leaders and the involvement of local officials. Aid to the environment 1: CSA and landscape management approaches promoted under the FS4FS support the protection of natural resources. Capacity Building 1: The Concern team works closely with diverse stakeholders for succession planning, ensuring that local communities and businesses retain skills, resources, and innovations. Cascading training mechanisms embed specialists, trainers, and lead farmers in the public and private sector, in counties and communities. Gender Equality 1: The programme takes a gender transformative approach – improving women’s independence, access to finances and decision-making, at the same time as engaging men. Nutrition 1:This outcome focuseson increased crop production and diversification, thus improving the nutritional status of HHS.
